title: GP-REG-032-v1.2 — Coupled Research Registers
note: Not held, and the refusal is the finding. This is the live coupled-register workbook, a native Google Sheet, which the 2026-09-17 inventory records at 1,345,511 bytes across 44 tabs. Fetched without an export MIME type it renders as text/csv: 30 lines and 9,277 bytes, the entry/control tab alone, whose own rows link to seven further tabs the export does not contain. Three distinct renderings of this one id exist in this session's transcripts -- two CSV exports of 9,277 bytes with different SHA-256, and a 1,919,741-byte XLSX export -- so the porter refused to pick one and stored nothing. The two CSV exports are the same length and differ in exactly one field. The 2026-09-18 fetches read "2952 catalog entries; 25 review routes; 22 exclusions/containers"; the 2026-09-20 fetch reads "2952 catalog entries; 34 review routes; 22 exclusions/containers". Every other byte of that row is identical, including its Updated UTC field, which reads 2026-09-17T17:19:16.450Z in both: the row's content moved while the row's own timestamp did not. Recorded, not repaired. Nothing here decides which rendering is the object, which review-route count is correct, or what the stamp should say. The exported registers under registers/ are regenerated from registers/source/ and are not touched by this observation. A reading copy of one tab of a 44-tab workbook would carry the whole workbook's title over a small fraction of its body, which is the second reason not to store one.
